page.title: Best NAS With Drives Included (2026): Synology BeeStation Plus vs UGREEN DH2300
page.desc: How much space a NAS with storage inside really gives you. The BeeStation Plus 8 TB keeps about 6.98 TB for files, while a mirrored 8 TB two-drive box keeps 4 TB. Plus the UGREEN DH2300 if you'd rather add your own drives.
page.answer: Short answer. For a NAS with storage already inside, get the Synology BeeStation Plus 8 TB: about 6.98 TB is usable for files. A mirrored 8 TB two-drive box keeps only 4 TB. The BeeStation has one drive, so keep a backup copy too.

page.after:
What the differences mean

  • BeeStation Plus 8 TB: 6.98 ÷ 8 = 87% of the label holds files, all on one drive.
  • BeeStation 4 TB: 3.45 ÷ 4 = 86% of the label.
  • Buffalo LinkStation 720D 8 TB (LS720D0802): two 4 TB drives that ship set to RAID 1, so 4 TB holds files (before formatting). That is 4 ÷ 8 = 50% of the label. The BeeStation Plus holds 6.98 ÷ 4 = about 1.7× as much, but it keeps no second copy.
  • Power per usable TB, in use: BeeStation Plus 14.75 W ÷ 6.98 TB = 2.11 W/TB; BeeStation 4 TB 7.84 W ÷ 3.45 TB = 2.27 W/TB. Running the Plus in use all year comes to 14.75 W × 8,760 h = 129 kWh; with the drive hibernating all year it is 2.83 W × 8,760 h = 25 kWh.
  • Price per bay, before drives (UGREEN store, 2026-11-17): DH2300 $239.99 ÷ 2 = $120.00; DH4300 Plus $373.99 ÷ 4 = $93.50.
  • Speed: on 2.5GbE, Macworld measured the DH4300 Plus at 206 MBps reads in RAID 1, against 99 MBps on gigabit (206 ÷ 99 = 2.1×). The 1GbE boxes stop near 100–112 MB/s.
Your useFits best
Storage inside, works out of the box, largest usable spaceBeeStation Plus 8 TB, plus a USB drive for a second copy
Small photo and document library, lowest powerBeeStation 4 TB
Two copies inside the box at the lowest box priceUGREEN DH2300 with two matching drives
Large video library, four drives, faster transfersUGREEN DH4300 Plus
Synology software with drives you chooseSynology DS225+

Labelled TB vs usable TB on a NAS with storage

The TB number on a drives-included NAS is the raw size of the drives. Two things shrink it. First, formatting and the system take a slice: Synology states about 6.98 TB usable for the 8 TB BeeStation Plus and about 3.45 TB for the 4 TB BeeStation. Second, a mirror stores every file twice. Buffalo's spec sheet for the LS720D0802 lists the drives as 4 TB × 2 and says the unit ships set to RAID 1. A mirror keeps one drive's worth, so an "8 TB" box holds 4 TB of files.

The mirror is the price of a second copy, and the BeeStation has none. Synology's own FAQ says the BeeStation has 'only one built-in hard drive (no RAID)' and that 'Data safety comes from backups, not RAID.' Its USB-A and USB-C ports take an external drive that the BeeStation can back up to automatically. Luka Manestar (Blackvoid) reports that the internal drive is fixed and the whole unit is replaced if it fails. So budget for a USB drive alongside {buy:synology-beestation-plus-8tb-bst170-8t}.

If you'd rather have the mirror inside the box, a diskless two-bay plus two matching drives does it, and you choose the drive size. The {buy:ugreen-nasync-dh2300} is the lowest-priced route at $239.99 before drives. NAS Compares measured it at about 9.5 W idle and 31–32 dBA with two 4 TB drives. On the Synology side, Synology's DSM 7.3 release says 2025-model-year DiskStation Plus units such as the DS225+ accept hard drives that Synology has not validated. M.2 storage pools still need drives on Synology's compatibility list.
